source_text:
Ὁ δὲ Ἡρακλέων τό· Ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων· οὕτω διηγήσατο· χαίρει μὲν γάρ, φησίν, ὁ σπείρων ὅτι σπείρει, καὶ ὅτι ἤδη τινὰ τῶν σπερμάτων αὐτοῦ συνάγεται· χαίρει δὲ καὶ ὁ θερίζων ὅτι θερίζει.

ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐδύναντο ἀμφότεροι ἅμα ἄρξασθαι· ἔδει γὰρ πρῶτον σπαρῆναι, εἶθ’ ὕστερον θερισθῆναι.
pass_a_gloss: But Heracleon explained the “In order that the one sowing together may rejoice and the one harvesting” thus: for the one sowing rejoices, he says, that he sows, and that already some of his seeds are gathered; and the one harvesting also rejoices that he harvests. But both were not able to begin at the same time; for it was necessary first to be sown, then later to be harvested.
pass_b_english: Heracleon explains [[“so that sower and reaper may rejoice together” >> Bible:John 4:36]] this way: the sower rejoices that he sows and that some of his seed is already gathered; the reaper rejoices that he reaps.
Yet both could not start at once: first must come sowing, then harvest.
